stage1.impression: A tidy, symmetrical night render of a long bar with a slatted timber wall and a lit band under the ceiling. It reads as CG straight away. The fluted band is salmon pink and blown out, so it looks like an LED sign. The oak has no grain, the leather is plastic, the bottles are copies of each other, the ceiling and right wall are flat black voids, and the pendants are white discs that light nothing below them. No EARF speaker is visible, so the only saturated colour is the band. As it stands a magazine would see a generic hospitality render rather than a specific, well-made place.

blocking_9: The lantern band reads as warm amber cast acrylic with visible fin edges and depth, not as a pink LED sign: clip_pct < 1 in [270,170,910,250] and delta_e to #E8A050 < 10
Pools of light fall on the quartzite bar top under each counter spot, with dark between them, and the stone shows veining at 1:1
The ceiling and right plaster wall hold readable detail (tone, texture, falloff) instead of empty black planes
The oak baffle, porch and banquette rail show real grain, tone variation between boards and fine end checks; the leather shows creasing and a soft sheen
No repeated copies: bottles vary in shape, height and fill, and the four identical bare tables get different props
Signs of life: drinks, a record out of its sleeve, a coat or bag on the banquette
The pendants glow (a lit diffuser with a gradient and a warm halo on the wall) instead of reading as flat white discs
Something specific to EARF reads in frame (a Core or Hemisphere in its tint, or a view into the porch), so this is Planet EARF and not any slat-wall bar

defects.what: Lantern band blown (7.2% clipped) and salmon pink (RGB 247/156/132, dE2000 21.5 from amber). The fins read as corrugated plastic sheet or signage, not thick cast acrylic.
A diagonal haze shaft from an unseen spot crosses the dark ceiling and the band, reading as a CG god ray
Ceiling is a featureless void (median 11.9), so the 4 m height and the structure are lost
Right plaster wall is a large flat dark plane (median 20.8) with no texture: dead weight in the right third
Quartzite bar top reads as flat dark grey slab with no pools under the 5 counter spots. The profile drops from 69 to 33 along x with no rhythm.
Hemisphere pendants are near-white discs with no gradient or halo and throw no visible pool on the counter
Back-bar bottles are visibly repeated instances of a few models at identical spacing
Oak baffle and porch boards are uniform and grainless, with a perfectly even tone per board, and read as a laminate texture. The black notch row at the porch head looks like a modelling gap.
Four identical bare tables in a perfect row, with one stock glass on two of them: a repeated model, a showroom
Banquette leather is smooth, sheenless plastic; the oak rail above it is the only real-looking timber in frame
Terrazzo counter face: the chips are oversized and uniform, reading as a speckle texture, and the base is near-crushed at the lower left
The grade is a single orange-brown cast over everything. Plaster, terrazzo and stone lose their own neutral colours, so the room reads as monochrome rather than warm-lit.

changes.problem: The lantern band is blown and pink, so it reads as an LED sign rather than lit amber cast acrylic.

evidence.measured: lum_median 174, clip_pct 7.23, RGB median 247/156/132, dE2000 21.5 vs #FFB347

change.setting: the lantern's band emission (and its colour)
change.to: 0.35, emitter colour 2200 K amber, with a slight top-to-bottom gradient (brighter at the fin roots) so the fin edges catch light

changes.expected: A warm amber glow that holds detail across the fins, unclipped, with the polished fin edges visible as brighter lines

changes.problem: The counter spots make no pools on the quartzite, so the bar top is a flat grey slab and the room has no rhythm of light and dark.

evidence.measured: lum_median 50, lum_p95 93; x-profile 69, 57, 56, 56, 33, 33, 37, 46 with no peaks

change.to: 45.0 W, 18.0 deg, each aimed at the top's centreline between stools, with a soft edge (blend 0.3)

changes.expected: Five readable pools on the stone with darker gaps, the glasses on the bar catching highlights, and the stone's veining legible inside the pools

changes.problem: The ceiling is an empty black void and a stray haze shaft cuts across it.

evidence.measured: lum_median 11.9, lum_range 17.7; diagonal shaft visible at [380,90,540,210]

change.to: fill 0.12 W/m2 aimed up as a soft bounce off the counter, haze 0.004 per m; mask the spot that makes the shaft out of the haze volume

changes.expected: The ceiling plane and its edges read faintly. No god-ray streak.

changes.problem: The right plaster wall is a large, flat, dark plane that wastes a fifth of the frame.

change.to: 16.0 W, 30.0 deg, tilted 10 deg toward the wall so each throws a scallop on the lime plaster above the rail

changes.expected: Scallops of light on the plaster with its trowel texture visible, falling off to dark between them; the banquette reads as a seat

changes.problem: Oak, leather and terrazzo read as CG textures at 1:1: grainless uniform boards, plastic leather, oversized uniform chips.

evidence.measured: baffle lum_range 80 with even tone per board; crop shows no grain

change.setting: the oak's tone and finish, the terrazzo's chip size, the leather finish
change.from: uniform oak tone, smooth leather, large uniform chips
change.to: oiled rift oak with real grain at scale and per-board tone varied by ±8%, satin roughness 0.45; leather with crease and roughness variation; terrazzo chips 3 to 12 mm mixed on a warm grey ground

changes.expected: Boards read as individual pieces of oak, the leather has a soft broken sheen, and the terrazzo reads as stone

changes.problem: Repeated models and no sign of life make it a showroom.

evidence.measured: four identical bare tables; back bar of a few repeated bottle models at even spacing

change.to: varied bottles (height, label tone, fill), two half-finished drinks and a napkin on the bar, a record out of its sleeve on the nearest table, a coat over the banquette, a candle on one table

changes.expected: A lived-in room with variety at 1:1 and small highlights scattered through the dark

changes.problem: One orange cast flattens every material to the same brown.
changes.expected: The lamps stay warm, but plaster, terrazzo and quartzite regain some neutral grey, so the warmth reads as light rather than a filter

changes.problem: The eye-level, near-symmetrical view gives the empty right wall and ceiling too much frame and keeps the lantern porch distant.

evidence.measured: right fifth median about 21; ceiling band median 12

change.to: [5.4, 2.4, 1.2] (seated) looking at [13.0, 4.0, 1.8], 32 mm, verticals kept true

changes.expected: The counter and porch fill more of the frame, less dead ceiling and wall, and a closer seated view like a magazine's

out_of_scope.request: Put an EARF speaker (the Tropos pair) in the frame as the hero and the only saturated colour
out_of_scope.why: The pair is fixed inside the lantern and this frame looks at the lantern's face, so the product cannot be moved. Unless a camera move sees into the porch, the brief's one-colour test cannot be met in this frame. The band is the colour instead, and c1 makes it read as amber acrylic.

out_of_scope.request: Thicker fins, or acrylic in the band set flush into an oak reveal
out_of_scope.why: The acrylic band's place and fins are fixed architecture

out_of_scope.request: Rework the porch head (the black notch row) so it reads as a joint, not a gap
out_of_scope.why: The porch is fixed as drawn. If the notches are a modelling error rather than the design, the owner should check them.
